key_insight: A new upper bound, log₂[1 + (1−γ)γ^(γ/(1−γ))], strictly tightens three established bounds on two-way-assisted amplitude-damping channel capacities for every 0<γ<1.
engineering_relevance: The bounds quantify fundamental limits on quantum communication, entanglement distribution, private communication, and secret-key agreement through relaxing qubits.
method: Extend sector teleportation simulation to qubits using phase rotations and permutations within fixed-excitation subspaces.
Determine exact additive resource entanglement and regularized entanglement gain at fixed input population.
Extend capacity bounds to thermal excitation using generalized amplitude damping.
evidence_signal: Analytical results establish strict improvements over the PLOB, analytic max-relative-entropy, and optimized balanced squashed-entanglement bounds; at high damping, a known triple-rail protocol achieves more than 99.54% of the new bound’s leading coefficient.
watch_item: The results are theoretical bounds, and the exact entanglement of generalized amplitude-damping resources remains unknown.
paper_title: Improved two-way capacity upper bounds for amplitude-damping channels
